$comment: U53 -- give the centre-panel SPI bus probe points. Review item 24.
The review filed this as ergonomics: zero test points and every via tented,
so nowhere to land a scope. It is more than that. The U9 read-integrity
soak is the project's own acceptance gate for every DASH_SPI_RUN_HZ
increase, and it is written against TP1=SCLK, TP2=MOSI, TP3=MISO, TP4=CS,
TP5=GND, with 'TP5 is a dedicated scope ground -- use it with a short ground
spring'. None of those existed, so the clock walk's 'scope TP1/TP3, ground
on TP5' branch could not be run as written. Those names come from Board2,
whose LVC-buffered topology Board3 dropped; the nets below are the Board3
equivalents.
PARTLY REFUTING THE FINDING FIRST: 'no bare ground reference' is not true.
MP1-MP4 are 5.00 x 5.00 mm bare-copper pads on /GND at the four board
corners (30,90), (30,130), (270,90), (270,130) -- mask open, no paste. They
are a perfectly good ground. What they are not is NEAR anything: the closest
is ~100 mm from the centre-panel SPI, which defeats the short-ground-spring
requirement that makes the measurement trustworthy. The gap is a LOCAL
ground beside the signals, and signal probe points at all.
NO NEW PARTS. Vias already exist on all four centre-panel SPI signals, and
a /GND via sits 2.03-5.20 mm from them, so opening the mask over five vias
buys the whole thing: no footprints, no BOM line, no CPL row, no schematic
symbol, and nothing for schematic parity to disagree with. The board default
tents every via front and back, which is right for the other 229.
The cluster spans x 148.43..152.46, y 91.95..96.81 -- about 4 x 5 mm, just
north-east of R32/R35 and south of FPC2, on the top layer.
TP1 SCLK  (152.460, 93.750)  /SCLK_C_MCU   5.06 mm from ground
TP2 MOSI  (149.750, 95.260)  /MOSI_C_MCU   2.03 mm
TWO HONEST LIMITATIONS, both worth knowing before trusting a trace.
1. TP1 and TP2 sit on the _MCU side of R32/R35, because /SCLK_C and /MOSI_C
have no via -- they are 4.3 mm top-only runs from the resistor to FPC2.
So those two show what the MCU LAUNCHES, not what the panel receives.
With source-series termination that is a half-amplitude step for one
round trip, which is correct behaviour and looks alarming if you expect
a full-swing edge. TP3 (MISO) and TP4 (CS) have no series element and
read directly. R32/R35 were left at the connector by U50, so probing the
panel side means touching the resistor's far pad.
2. A 0.6 mm via is a small target. It takes a fine tip and a sprung ground
lead, not an alligator clip. For a bigger ground, MP1-MP4 are still there.
THIS COSTS TWO silk_over_copper WARNINGS, KNOWINGLY. Opening the mask at
TP3 and TP4 clips a notch out of R41's and FPC2's silk outlines, taking the
board from 0 violations to 2 warnings at --severity-all. Errors, unconnected
and schematic parity all stay 0.
Accepted rather than designed around, and the alternative was measured, not
assumed. Both nets have a second via that IS silk-clear -- /MISO_C at
8.85 mm from the ground via instead of 3.83 and 5.20 mm. This project's own
clock-walk procedure says why that is the wrong trade: 'TP5 is a dedicated
scope ground -- use it with a short ground spring, or the ringing on screen
will be the probe's inductance, not the board's.' Ground-lead inductance is
the documented failure mode of this exact measurement, so doubling the ground
reach to keep two silk outlines intact would be optimising the wrong thing.
The warning is also not describing damage. silk_over_copper means the fab
will clip silkscreen off exposed copper -- which is correct behaviour over a
probe point, since silk ink does not belong on bare copper. The visible
result is a ~0.6 mm gap in two component outlines.
Not silk-labelled, because kicad_handroute.py has no silk-text operation --
the same gap that blocks review items 26 and 27. Until that exists, these
five are identified by coordinate here and in the triage doc, and by eye as
the only bare copper in that area.

steps.step: 1/1  open the mask over five vias -> TP1..TP5 for the U9 soak
